analysis: The broad response uses the law gateway, rights, criminal law, comparative private and constitutional law, public international law and EU law as a coherent comparative-law spine. Political institutions, social analysis, research and economics contextualise law. Groningen’s cumulative Dutch civil, administrative and criminal procedure and courtroom capstone remain substantive gaps.

International/public law retains genuine EU, international, comparative constitutional and human-rights study. International relations, conflict, state formation, public economics and empirical social inquiry deepen the institutional perspective.

Technology/governance combines the comparative-law spine with ethical issues of fairness and privacy, software/data literacy, public policy and cross-border business regulation. There is genuine law and technology substance without a dedicated UCR sequence in Dutch technology regulation. Introduction to Data Science now precedes Machine Learning.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce legal systems and legal reasoning. UCR compares traditions and considers law in society.
Both examine fundamental rights. UCR considers human-rights traditions and international protection, alongside comparative material.
Both address criminal liability and core principles. UCR uses comparative examples and a simulated legal aid clinic; Groningen teaches Dutch criminal doctrine in a cumulative sequence.
Both address sources, international legal subjects, jurisdiction and responsibility.
Both examine constitutional institutions and public power. Groningen focuses on the Dutch constitutional order.
Both study private-law principles. UCR compares property, tort and contract across jurisdictions; Groningen teaches Dutch civil law.
Both examine EU institutions, the EU legal order and the internal market.
Both study commercial law and contractual relationships. UCR focuses on business across borders.
Both consider how incentives and public rules affect economic outcomes. UCR covers public intervention and welfare rather than the full law-and-economics course.
Groningen requires Strafrecht 2; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Burgerlijk Recht 2; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Romeins Recht; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Arbeid en Zekerheid; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Burgerlijk Procesrecht; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Strafrecht 3; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Bestuursrecht: Rechtsbescherming; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires Burgerlijk Recht 3; the selected UCR curricula do not contain an equivalent dedicated Dutch-law component.
Groningen requires one introductory legal philosophy or legal sociology course. UCR offers related general philosophy and sociology.
Groningen continues the legal foundations sequence and includes a computing practical for law students.
Groningen introduces Dutch administrative law. UCR covers selected administrative topics within broader legal courses.
Groningen studies the Dutch parliament and constitution. UCR political science courses provide related context.
Groningen studies administrative decisions under Dutch law.
Groningen introduces research using legal sources and methods. UCR provides broader empirical research training.
Groningen teaches legal history. UCR history courses primarily cover wider social and political history.
Groningen students write a legal publication. UCR research training uses other disciplinary methods.
The Groningen capstone integrates legal writing and a hearing. UCR’s optional independent research is a separate opportunity.

academicConstruction: Screened current GOSLAWJ offerings for private, public, criminal, rights and EU coverage and supporting GOSPOLI and DIS/BEN courses for technology and government. Rescheduled Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Economics and Business & Economy in the Age of AI. Option three replaces introductory rhetoric with Public Policy Analysis, which adds institutional case analysis and policy memos in an available semester. Removed forced matches between legal research, administrative doctrine and courtroom training and broader social science courses.
